- numpy - matplotlib import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np ''' function which returns the force for specific coordinates ''' def forceV(x, y, z, strength): Fx = -strength * x Fy = -strength * y Fz = -strength * z return Fx, Fy, Fz ''' initial conditions of the motion ''' v0x = 14 v0y = 0 v0z = 0 x0 = 2 y0 = 0 z0 = 0 ''' define time interval via number of intervals and increment ''' dt = 0.05 Nt = 1530 timeinterval = np.arange(0, Nt * dt, dt) ''' define properties of the particle and force ''' mass = 0.3 springstiffness = 20.1 ''' solve Newton's equation of motion recursively ''' pos = [[x0, y0, z0]] vel = [] vel1x = v0x + (dt / 2) * forceV(pos[-1][0], pos[-1][1], pos[-1][2], springstiffness)[0] / mass vel1y = v0y + (dt / 2) * forceV(pos[-1][0], pos[-1][1], pos[-1][2], springstiffness)[1] / mass vel1z = v0z + (dt / 2) * forceV(pos[-1][0], pos[-1][1], pos[-1][2], springstiffness)[2] / mass vel.append([vel1x, vel1y, vel1z]) for nt in range(1, Nt): x1 = pos[-1][0] + dt * vel[-1][0] y1 = pos[-1][1] + dt * vel[-1][1] z1 = pos[-1][2] + dt * vel[-1][2] pos.append([x1, y1, z1]) force = forceV(pos[-1][0] / (nt * dt)**2, pos[-1][1] / (nt * dt)**2, pos[-1][2] / (nt * dt)**2, springstiffness) v1x = vel[-1][0] + dt * force[0] / mass v1y = vel[-1][1] + dt * force[1] / mass v1z = vel[-1][2] + dt * force[2] / mass vel.append([v1x, v1y, v1z]) fig, ax = plt.subplots() #ax.set_xlim(0, rmax) #ax.set_ylim(-20, 20) ax.plot(timeinterval, np.array(pos)[:, 0], label=r'$m=1\,$kg and $c=1\,\frac{kg}{s^2}$') ax.set(xlabel=r'time', ylabel=r'x coordinate', title=r'$\vec{F}=-c\,\vec{r}$') ax.grid() plt.legend(loc='best', numpoints=1) #fig.savefig("myfirstnumericaltrajectory.svg") #fig.savefig("myfirstnumericaltrajectory.pdf") fig
